applies_why: The text decides a collision in which each side's press is its own chain read together ([CR2] answering with 8:8 and 9:6-7 against [DR3]'s chain of the sign's bounds), which is exactly the situation K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: Phrase read: 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.' Reading 1: a judge breaches whenever its decisive ground is one verse's own silence, even if a debater's chain (DR3's link that the sign announces without explaining) voices the same point. Reading 2: a judge is clean if it merely restates a debater's chain claim without resting the verdict on the single verse. I weighed Reading 1, because the verdict's only stated ground is the sign's own failure to state the mechanism, not any footing comparison of the two chains the judge had just named.
why: Having named both chains, the judge rested its verdict on the ground that one verse, the sign itself, does not state the mechanism in its own words, which is the retired stating-verse test and a verse-by-verse decision instead of the required weighing of chain against chain by footing.
